config.fetchMetaTitle: Fetch the icon and title for this URL
config.appliesToTitle: These settings only take effect for bookmarks set to this mode
config.statusModesLead: Each bookmark is set to one of three modes, in its own editor or with a right-click on the dashboard. The settings on this tab decide how those checks are carried out.
config.statusModesWhere: Set a bookmark’s mode under Bookmarks → Edit, or right-click it on the dashboard.
config.statusBrowserChecksNote: How the dashboard tests the bookmarks on screen while you have it open. Applies to bookmarks set to Periodic or Monitor; a bookmark set to Off is never tested.
config.statusServerChecksNote: Re-tests bookmarks on the server, so the Health view stays current without anyone having the dashboard open. Off by default because it makes outbound requests.
config.statusAlertsNote: Posts to a webhook when a monitored bookmark goes down and again when it recovers. Only monitored bookmarks raise alerts — Periodic flags a broken link in the Health view but never notifies.
config.statsNoActivity: No bookmarks were used in this period.
config.statsNeverOpenedHint: Candidates to tidy up — they have never been used.
config.statsAllOpened: Everything has been opened at least once.
config.statsScoreHint: Starts at 100 and loses points for bookmarks you never open, links gone stale, duplicate URLs and clashing shortcuts.
config.overviewNothingToDo: Nothing needs attention — everything checks out.
config.overviewUpdateAvailableBody: You are running {current}. {latest} is available on GitHub.
config.overviewNewFeatureCaptureTitle: Save a link from your phone, or from any browser
config.overviewNewFeatureCaptureWhat: Saving a link meant being at a desktop with the extension installed. On a phone, or in Safari or Firefox, there was no way in at all — you mailed yourself the link and dealt with it later, which is how links get lost.
config.overviewNewFeatureCaptureEnable: Nothing to switch on. If this install asks for a password, set a capture key on the server and paste it into the panel — it opens these two routes and nothing else.
config.overviewNewFeatureLogRebuildTitle: The server log says what it is doing
config.overviewNewFeatureLogRebuildWhat: The log was a wall of lines with no way to tell a note from a failure, and whole parts of the server said nothing at all — a check round, a feed poll, an import, a saved copy, a scheduled backup, a write to disk that did not work. When something went wrong there was nothing to read, and when nothing went wrong there was no way to watch it work.
config.overviewNewFeatureLogRebuildHow: Every line now says how serious it is and which part of nextDash it came from, in a sentence written for someone running it rather than reading its source. Detail level chooses how much is written — Quiet, Normal or Verbose — and takes effect on the very next line, with no restart. Activity trail beside it picks which twelve things are recorded in machine-readable form.
config.overviewNewFeatureLogRebuildEnable: Switch on Collect server log to read it in the app; the container log has it either way.
config.overviewNewFeatureServerLogTitle: Read the server log without leaving nextDash
config.overviewNewFeatureServerLogWhat: When something went wrong there was nothing to look at. Finding out why an import failed or a link check never ran meant reaching the machine nextDash runs on.
config.overviewNewFeatureServerLogEnable: Nothing to switch on. Limit it by age or by number of entries, and clear the whole lot whenever you like.
config.overviewNewFeatureServerLogHow: Data & backups › Server log lists what the server has been doing, keeps itself up to date every few seconds if you want, and colours warnings and errors so they are easy to spot. Search looks through everything kept.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetMenuTitle: A widget answers to the right-click and the keyboard
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetMenuWhat: Renaming a widget or changing its width meant leaving the dashboard for Config → Widgets to find the switch, and the keyboard stepped around widgets rather than into them — they were the one block on the page arrow keys could not enter.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetMenuHow: Right-click a widget title for rename, one column or two, fold, settings and close. Arrow keys now step inside and move through its rows the way they move through a category, Enter opens the row under the cursor, and every action in the menu has a key of its own.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthIgnoreTitle: A bookmark can stop reporting one condition
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthIgnoreWhat: A link you have already looked at and decided is fine kept being flagged as stale, unused or broken on every visit. The only ways to quiet it were to delete the bookmark or to stop checking it, and both throw away more than the flag.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthIgnoreHow: Press n or z on a row in Health, or use its menu, to set one flag aside. The bookmark stays in your collection and keeps being checked — it simply stops raising that condition. The Ignored filter lists everything set aside, and one click puts a bookmark back.
config.overviewNewFeatureDuplicateWhereTitle: A link you already have is found wherever it is
config.overviewNewFeatureDuplicateWhereWhat: The duplicate check looked only at the page you were saving to. The same link filed on Work went straight in again from Personal, and the duplicates report found it weeks later — which is reporting a problem rather than preventing it.
config.overviewNewFeatureDuplicateWhereEnable: Nothing to switch on. The add form, quick add and the browser extension all ask it the same way.
config.overviewNewFeatureRotReportTitle: Link rot, as something you can watch happen
config.overviewNewFeatureRotReportWhat: A broken link was only ever broken — not broken since May, not broken and never opened, not one of forty on the same dead host. And a page that answers 200 while saying “not found” read as perfectly healthy.
config.overviewNewFeatureRotReportEnable: Spotting a page that says “not found” costs one bounded read per check, so it is a switch under Behavior → Status & health. The rest is on.
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSessionTitle: Ten links, two minutes — cleaning that ends
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSessionWhat: Work through is the best thing in the health view, and it was reachable only from a health filter, by someone who had already decided to do maintenance. Deciding is the hard part, and a filter holding forty-seven rows is a number people learn to ignore.
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSessionEnable: Nothing to switch on. Below five waiting links the card stays quiet.
config.overviewNewFeatureFreshTitle: Fresh — the bookmarks that have something new
config.overviewNewFeatureFreshWhat: Today, Recently opened, Most used and Stale all answer a question about what you did. None of them could answer the one you actually have in front of a wall of links: which of these is worth opening right now?
config.overviewNewFeatureFreshEnable: Off by default, under Behavior → Fresh. Switching it on checks once immediately; the feeds themselves were already found while previews were fetched, so nothing has to be re-fetched.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStableListTitle: The health list stays still while you work through it
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStableListWhat: Health asks you to open a link and see for yourself, and then charged you for it: never opened and not opened in 30 days each cost ten points, so the first open raised the row’s score and the worst-first order carried it away. On a list of two hundred that meant tenth place became a hundred and eighty-eighth, while you were still reading it.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStableListEnable: Nothing to switch on. The score breakdown behind the badge now separates what costs points from what is only worth knowing.
config.overviewNewFeatureTypeThenEnterWhat: A bookmark shortcut fired the moment what you had typed matched it exactly, so an ordinary word was swallowed halfway through: "invoice" opened something at "in" and left "voice" behind. Words starting with g, j or k lost their first letter to the grid keys instead. Which of your words survived depended on which other bookmarks you happened to own, and changed every time you added one.
config.overviewNewFeatureTypeThenEnterEnable: Nothing to switch on. A short key legend appears under the bookmarks after your first keystroke and goes again when you open something — switch it off under Behavior → General, where shortcut hints on the toolbar icons now start off as well.
config.overviewNewFeatureFailureReasonTitle: A failed check says why, and one miss is not an outage
config.overviewNewFeatureFailureReasonWhat: A name that would not resolve, a connection that timed out and one that was refused were all stored the same way — not up, no code — so the outage list, the timeline and the export showed no cause at all for anything that was not an HTTP error. And a single dropped check counted as downtime for a month afterwards.
config.overviewNewFeatureFailureReasonEnable: Nothing to switch on. The trend chart can draw broken, stale, unchecked or the score instead of only healthy, a whole selection can be muted at once, and the three-second limit on a check is now a setting under Behavior → Status & health.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxCountsTitle: The inbox counts what you can see
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxCountsWhat: A search or a site filter narrowed the list and left the tiles, the pills and the badge counting everything, so the numbers on screen described a different set of links than the one in front of you. Mark all read reached links you could not see, and a sleeping link was invisible until the day it came back.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxCountsEnable: Nothing to switch on. Import now sits beside the CSV and JSON exports: it skips links that are already there and says afterwards how many arrived, how many were already in and how many did not fit.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpreadTitle: A category can span several columns
config.overviewNewFeatureSpreadWhat: A category with forty bookmarks in it towered over everything beside it, and everything past the items-per-category limit sat behind a "+ N more" you had to click every visit. One long category was enough to make a page feel lopsided.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpreadEnable: Right-click a category header and pick Spread across columns, or press Shift+W on it. Pages & tags → Categories has the same switch on every row. It needs an items-per-category limit — spreading is unavailable while that is set to Unlimited.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkUndoTitle: A way back out of a bulk delete
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkUndoWhat: Removing fifteen bookmarks at once had no way back except digging them out of the trash one at a time. And if the save did not go through, the rows disappeared from the screen anyway with nothing to tell you they were still there.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkUndoEnable: Nothing to switch on. Tick some rows with x, or Alt-click them, and Delete asks once for the whole set.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksMenuWhat: Everything you can do to a bookmark here was spread across the buttons on the row and the toolbar above the list, and which of them applied to the row you were pointing at was not always obvious.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksMenuEnable: Nothing to switch on. Shift and right-click still gives you the browser menu.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkSettingsWhat: Every choice this section made was made for you and could not be changed: the sort reset on every visit, fifty rows loaded at a time whatever your screen, and a quick-added bookmark always arrived unchecked, unpinned and without a category.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkSettingsEnable: Nothing to switch on. Every setting starts at exactly the value that used to be fixed, so nothing changes until you change it.
config.overviewNewFeatureUsageDataTitle: Ask when you added something, or last opened it
config.overviewNewFeatureUsageDataWhat: nextDash records when you add a bookmark, when you last opened it and how often — and none of it could be reached from the search bar or from a collection of your own. "Added this month and never opened since" was not a question you could ask.
config.overviewNewFeatureUsageDataEnable: The search filters work straight away. Recently added is off until you switch it on, and takes its own limit and pages.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowKeysTitle: Four more things you can do without the mouse
config.overviewNewFeatureRowKeysWhat: Pinning, sharing, opening a bookmark in Health and filtering to a tag you can see all needed the mouse or the command palette, in an app where everything else on a row has a key.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowKeysEnable: Nothing to switch on. Press ! or F1 for the full list, which is also on the printable cheat sheet.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowTagsTitle: Tags on the bookmark rows themselves
config.overviewNewFeatureRowTagsWhat: Every row already carried its tags and showed none of them, so the one place you could not act on a bookmark’s tag was the row in front of you.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowTagsEnable: Off by default, under Appearance → Display. Category headers also give back their width: the sort in use stays in front and the rest move behind a ⋯.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxTagsTitle: Tags on inbox links, at last
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxTagsWhat: Links saved with tags — from the browser extension, or captured with a tag already on them — kept those tags and showed you none of them. You could not see them, change them, or search for them.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxTagsEnable: Nothing to switch on. Any link that already had tags shows them from now on.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxStatsTitle: How much of the Inbox you actually use
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxStatsWhat: An inbox is easy to fill and easy to stop emptying. Whether the links you save become bookmarks or quietly pile up was not something the view could tell you.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxStatsEnable: Nothing to switch on. The figures cover the whole life of your inbox.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpacingTitle: Decide how much room the grid gives away
config.overviewNewFeatureSpacingWhat: The gap between category rows and the empty band down both edges were both fixed, and on a wide screen they added up to a lot of nothing.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpacingEnable: Page margins start exactly where they always were. Category spacing is a little tighter than before — pick Airy for the old gap.
config.overviewNewFeatureStructureTrashTitle: Deleted pages and categories come back
config.overviewNewFeatureStructureTrashWhat: Deleting a page took its bookmarks with it and kept nothing anywhere, so the more one click destroyed, the less you could recover.
config.overviewNewFeatureStructureTrashEnable: Nothing to switch on. The delete toast also offers Undo for eight seconds, and a page returns to its original slot rather than as a copy nothing points at.
config.overviewNewFeatureCategoryGridTitle: Add a category from the grid itself
config.overviewNewFeatureCategoryGridWhat: Making a category meant going into Config or through the bookmark form — both things you did on the way to something else.
config.overviewNewFeatureCategoryGridEnable: Nothing to switch on. Right-click a category header to rename or delete it, and a category you just made stays visible even with “hide empty categories” on.
config.overviewNewFeaturePageOverviewTitle: Make a page from the pages overview
config.overviewNewFeaturePageOverviewWhat: Adding a page lived in Config, away from the list of pages you were already looking at.
config.overviewNewFeaturePageOverviewEnable: Nothing to switch on. Creating takes you straight to the new page, which is where its first category gets added anyway.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkTitle: Fix a whole list of broken links at once
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkWhat: Health lists exactly what a clear-out starts from — broken, duplicate, stale — and then made you repair them one row at a time.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkEnable: Nothing to switch on. Deletes go to the trash, and a row that changed since the report was built is skipped rather than deleted.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkTagsWhat: Tagging worked one bookmark at a time, so putting the same tag on eight rows meant eight rounds.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkTagsEnable: Nothing to switch on. Clicking a tag the whole selection already has takes it off instead; setting a category lives in the Move button beside it.
config.overviewNewFeatureFormCreateTitle: Make a page or category while adding a bookmark
config.overviewNewFeatureFormCreateWhat: Filing a bookmark somewhere that did not exist yet meant leaving the half-filled form, making the page or category in Config, and starting over.
config.overviewNewFeatureFormCreateEnable: Nothing to switch on. A category is made on whichever page the form is pointing at, including one you created moments earlier.
config.overviewNewFeatureMultiSelectTitle: Select several bookmarks with x and X
config.overviewNewFeatureMultiSelectWhat: Bulk move and bulk delete used to live in the tag filter, so acting on several bookmarks meant they had to share a tag. Any rows will do now — x ticks one, X takes a whole category.
config.overviewNewFeatureMultiSelectEnable: Nothing to switch on. A toolbar appears with Move, Open, Copy links and Delete; Escape clears the selection.
config.overviewNewFeatureTrashWhat: Deleting a bookmark used to be final. It now goes to a trash and stays there for 30 days before going for good.
config.overviewNewFeatureTrashEnable: On by default, and it covers every delete — including a bulk delete of twenty rows at once. Under Config → Data & backups → Trash.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthContextMenuWhat: The nine actions behind a health row’s More button were reachable only by hovering the row and finding the button.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthContextMenuEnabl: Nothing to switch on — it is simply there. The ⋯ button and the m key keep working as before.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorEmphasisWhat: A bookmark set to Monitor now shows its status on the dashboard, the way a Periodic one always did — and you can say how much it should stand out.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorEmphasisEnable: Set to draw the eye only when something is down. Choose Always or Never under Config → Behavior → Status & health.
config.overviewNewFeatureSideRailWhat: The add, search, commands, and finders buttons can float center-bottom, dock into either bottom corner, or stand as a vertical rail down the left edge.
config.overviewNewFeatureSideRailEnable: The side rail keeps the space under your bookmarks clear, which pays off on wide screens.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormColumnsTit: The add-bookmark form fits on the screen
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormColumnsWha: Eleven fields under each other made the form 735 pixels tall, more than a laptop browser leaves below its tabs — so it scrolled and the save button sat under the fold. On a wide window the fields sit in two columns now: what the bookmark is on the left, where it goes and whether it is watched on the right, about 435 pixels in all.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormColumnsHow: Add a bookmark with + or Shift+B. Pinned, the availability buttons and every warning explain themselves in a small bubble on the control, on hover, on focus or on tap — so a clashing shortcut no longer pushes the fields down as you type.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormColumnsEna: Nothing to switch on. On a phone the fields stay in one column and Icon and Note are left out, keeping whatever the bookmark already had.
config.overviewNewFeatureSiteNewsFeedTitle: Posts from nextdash.cc, on your overview
config.overviewNewFeatureSiteNewsFeedWhat: The project writes about what it ships. Those posts now sit in the overview's news stream beside the releases, so a dashboard you already open tells you what changed instead of you going to look.
config.overviewNewFeatureSiteNewsFeedHow: Your server fetches the feed — the page never contacts another host, and nothing about you goes out with it. The chips above the stream hide the site's posts with one click if you would rather not see them.
config.overviewNewFeatureSiteNewsFeedEnable: On by default, and Behavior → Privacy → Show posts from nextdash.cc switches it off entirely: the request is then never made. DISABLE_NEWS_FEED=true does the same for a whole server.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardHealthTitle: The hover card knows what nextDash knows
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardHealthWhat: A preview used to be the page's own title and description — the same thing any browser could show you. The card now adds what only this dashboard knows: when the link was last checked and how fast it answered, uptime over thirty days, a certificate about to expire, how many times you have opened it and when.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardHealthHow: Hover a bookmark. Uptime and an expiring certificate show on hover, not only on a card you pinned with Shift+V — the health report is already loaded, so it costs no request.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardHealthEnabl: Appearance → Display → Link preview cards. A checklist decides which rows the card carries, so a reader who monitors nothing never sees a status row.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardModesTitle: Peek, pin, or turn the card off
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardModesWhat: Hovering gives you something to read: the card takes no pointer events and carries no buttons, so it never has to be chased. Shift+V pins one instead — it takes focus, carries Copy, Refresh and Edit, and closes on Escape.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardModesHow: Three modes rather than a switch: Off, On hover, and Keyboard only for people who want what the card says without one appearing under the pointer. The hover delay starts calm at 250 ms, so a card does not open on rows you were only passing over.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardModesEnable: Appearance → Display → Link preview cards, where the mode, the delay and the checklist sit together with a live sample.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeEngineTitle: A theme browser, and every theme rebuilt
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeEngineWhat: There are 214 built-in themes and they arrived as a listbox of 214 alphabetically sorted lines — which puts a theme twenty positions from its own other half, shows nothing of what any of them look like, and cannot be searched. At that size a list is not navigation.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeEngineHow: It is a grid of cards now: one per family with a light/dark switch on it, so 214 becomes 107, with search, segments for light, dark and favourites, and a star per family. Behind it every theme has been given an accent of its own instead of borrowing the success colour, a depth layer so a card sits on a surface rather than beside a border, and an improved backdrop you can set to dots, grid, lines or hatch. Thirty-three new families came with it.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemeEngineEnable: Nothing to switch on. Depth starts on rich and flat is the dashboard exactly as it was, so the old look is one control away.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkFetchTitle: Three slow jobs, done to a whole selection
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkFetchWhat: Rebuilding a preview, refreshing a favicon and keeping a copy of a page on disk were each on a single row's menu. A filter that finds forty bookmarks with no preview is exactly the case for doing them at once.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkFetchHow: Tick rows in the health view and the bulk bar offers all three. They run one request at a time behind a bar that counts, because each fetches a page belonging to somebody else. Saving copies asks first and names how many, since that one is minutes rather than seconds.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkFetchEnable: Nothing to switch on. Saving a copy needs monolith installed; the run says so on the first row rather than failing forty times.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsTitle: Your dashboard can show more than links
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsWhat: A page holds categories of bookmarks. It can now also hold widgets: eight kinds of tile reading data this install already keeps — uptime per monitored service, a thirty-day trend, what is waiting in the inbox, what you saved and never opened, which import failed, which feed went quiet, which certificate is running out.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsHow: Add and name them under Config → Widgets, then drag them into place among your categories like any other block. Each has its own settings: which page it counts, how many rows it shows, one column or two. A ninth type points at any address that answers with JSON, so a service that is not in the list needs no code.
config.overviewNewFeatureWidgetsEnable: Nothing to switch on. A new widget says what it is for before you add it, and a tile that leaves rows out says how many.
config.overviewNewFeatureSourcesTitle: Bookmarks that keep arriving on their own
config.overviewNewFeatureSourcesWhat: An import reads a file once. A source is a place bookmarks keep coming from and is asked again: GitHub stars, Raindrop.io, Hacker News, YouTube and Mastodon. The last three need no token at all — a username or a channel is the whole setup.
config.overviewNewFeatureSourcesHow: Config → Data & backups → Sources. Each source previews what it would write before writing it, remembers where it got to so a second run brings only what is new, and says what the last round did. The Sources widget puts that on your dashboard, which is where a failed import becomes visible without going looking for it.
config.overviewNewFeatureSourcesEnable: Nothing on by default. GitHub and Raindrop want a token; the other three want a name.
config.overviewNewFeatureArchiveTitle: A copy of the page, for when the page is gone
config.overviewNewFeatureArchiveWhat: The health view tells you a link is dead and offers whatever copy somebody else happened to take — which for a page nobody else bookmarked is usually none. nextDash can now ask for one on the day you save the link, and keep one on your own disk.
config.overviewNewFeatureArchiveHow: Config → Data & backups → Sources. Archive new bookmarks asks the Web Archive; archive.today is the second opinion for pages the first was not allowed to keep; and Local copies saves a whole page — text, styling and images — as one file in your data directory. Config → Bookmarks → Local copies lists what you have, grouped by the bookmark it belongs to.
config.overviewNewFeatureArchiveEnable: Off by default. The Web Archive accepts captures without keys at a smaller daily allowance; a key pair from archive.org lifts it.
config.overviewNewFeatureWebhooksTitle: Tell the rest of your machine what happened here
config.overviewNewFeatureWebhooksWhat: Everything nextDash talks to, it talks to on its own schedule, so anything built around it had to poll. Now a bookmark added, changed or removed — and a monitored link going down or coming back — is pushed to whatever you have built: an automation, a script, a home dashboard.
config.overviewNewFeatureWebhooksHow: Config → Data & backups → Webhooks. Name a receiver, give it an address, tick the events it should hear about. Every delivery is signed, so the receiver can tell it came from your install; the signing key is shown once, in the answer to the save that made it. On the same tab, an MCP endpoint lets an AI assistant search your bookmarks and add one.
config.overviewNewFeatureWebhooksEnable: Both off until you set them up. The assistant endpoint reads everything you have filed, which is why it starts closed.
config.overviewNewFeatureAddressBarTitle: Search your bookmarks from the browser's address bar
config.overviewNewFeatureAddressBarWhat: Typing a keyword, Tab, a term and Enter is how every other search-capable site is reached without opening it first. nextDash could not be reached that way at all — there was no address a search could live at.
config.overviewNewFeatureAddressBarHow: Visit your dashboard once and your browser picks it up: Firefox offers it under Search shortcuts, Chrome and its relatives under Site search, where you can shorten the keyword to something like nd. A search now has an address of its own too, so a particular search can be bookmarked or shared like any other view.
config.overviewNewFeatureAddressBarEnable: Nothing to switch on here — the keyword is set in your browser's own settings.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthTilesWhat: Certificates sat in a row of tiles that all narrow the list and was the one that did nothing when clicked — the count is hosts rather than bookmarks, which is a reason a reader cannot see. It opens the bookmarks on those hosts now.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthTilesHow: And Missing preview has a button that can empty it: Re-check and Retest all ask whether a link still answers, never what its page says, so the number could not move. Fetch previews asks every page for its title, description and image.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthTilesEnable: Nothing to switch on. Fetching is one request per bookmark, so it asks before it starts.
config.overviewNewFeatureFontSizeTitle: Try a font size before you take it
config.overviewNewFeatureFontSizeWhat: Hovering a size shows it on the dashboard behind the panel, so you see the choice at full size rather than a word describing it. Until v1.3.3.2 the panel resized with it and the button slid out from under the pointer — with a mouse the size was effectively unpickable.
config.overviewNewFeatureFontSizeHow: Appearance, at the top: five sizes, each drawn in the size it sets. Point at one to see the dashboard take it, click to keep it. The panel holds its own scale while you are trying them out and takes the new one when you choose.
config.overviewNewFeatureFontSizeEnable: Nothing to switch on. The size is per device unless you share settings across devices.
config.overviewNewFeatureNewsStreamTitle: One list for what the project is doing
config.overviewNewFeatureNewsStreamWhat: The overview used to answer "what is new" three times over: a panel showing one feature at a time out of forty-nine, a release summary repeating the line above it, and the project's posts below both — out of sight on most screens. It is one dated list now: posts from nextdash.cc, releases, and the settings each release introduced, newest first, every row saying where it came from.
config.overviewNewFeatureNewsStreamEnable: On by default. Your server fetches the site's feed a few times a day and your browser never contacts it; Behavior → Privacy switches that half off, and the rest of the list still works with no network at all.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardTitle: The hover card says what you know about a link
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardWhat: It printed the address twice, left out whether you had ever opened the bookmark, and slid away as you moved toward it. It now answers three things in the same order every time: what the page is, what it says, and what you already know about it — whether it answered and how quickly, how available it has been, a certificate about to expire, anything newly published, how often you open it, its shortcut and where it lives.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardEnable: On hover is the new default. Appearance → Display → Link preview cards offers off and keyboard only as well, a hover delay, and a checklist of the lines the card may draw — with the card itself beside it, drawn from one of your own bookmarks.
config.overviewNewFeatureButtonBarTabTitle: The button bar is one tab, not two
config.overviewNewFeatureButtonBarTabWhat: Where the bar sits was a panel on Layout; which buttons it carries were two panels on Toolbar & tabs, two tabs further along. Moving the bar and hiding a button on it were separate errands, and the second one was usually found by accident.
config.overviewNewFeatureButtonBarTabEnable: Nothing moved on screen — only where the settings live. Hiding a button still leaves its keyboard shortcut working, and :buttonbar moves the bar without opening config at all.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormWhat: Add and edit bookmarks in one centered modal — from the dashboard, Health, Inbox, Config, and search.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormEnable: Press ! for the full cheat sheet. Edit a row with ; or from Health and Inbox action bars.
config.overviewNewFeatureUpdateCheckWhat: nextDash can compare your running version with GitHub once a day — a dot on ★, a toast while you are actively using the app, and a manual check in the ★ modal and Config → Overview.
config.overviewNewFeatureUpdateCheckEnable: On by default under Config → Behavior → Privacy. Turn off Check GitHub for new releases if you prefer no outbound request.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksFiltersWhat: Search, filter, and sort the full bookmark library from one list — with chips that show what is active and summary tiles that follow your filters.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksFiltersEnable: Open Config → Bookmarks. Scroll to load more rows; press o or double-click a row to open its URL.
config.overviewNewFeaturePagesTagsTabsWhat: Pages & tags now opens on Categories, with Tags right beside it — the two lists you reach for most often.
config.overviewNewFeaturePagesTagsTabsEnable: Open Config → Pages & tags — Categories is selected by default.
config.overviewNewFeatureRandomThemeWhat: Let nextDash pick a different built-in theme from the pool instead of always showing your saved choice. Your saved theme remains the default whenever random is off.
config.overviewNewFeatureRandomThemeEnable: Open Config → Appearance → Theme and set Random theme to the mode you want.
config.overviewNewFeatureKeyboardWhat: Move through every config section, sub-tab, and list from the keyboard — no mouse required.
config.overviewNewFeatureKeyboardEnable: Press ! for the full cheat sheet, or open Help → Config navigation.
config.overviewNewFeatureFindSettingsWhat: Jump straight to any config section, sub-tab, help topic, or field you have visited.
config.overviewNewFeatureFindSettingsEnable: The shortcut works on every config section; the nav button is always below Help.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkPagesWhat: Each page keeps its own category list. The Bookmarks filter shows only categories for the page you pick.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkPagesEnable: Open Config → Bookmarks and use the page filter at the top of the list.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitoringTitle: Watch a bookmark, not just check it
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitoringWhat: A status check told you a link was broken the next time you happened to look. It could not tell you a site had been down all night, how often it goes down, or that its certificate expires on Friday.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitoringEnable: Per bookmark, from the Health view. Alerts, check cadence and maintenance windows live on this tab.
config.overviewNewFeatureWorkThroughTitle: Clear the Health list one bookmark at a time
config.overviewNewFeatureWorkThroughWhat: Filtering to Broken tells you what is wrong and then leaves every fix costing the same three moves: find the row again after the list redraws, aim at its action, decide.
config.overviewNewFeatureWorkThroughEnable: Nothing to switch on. It works on whatever the current filter shows.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemePreviewTitle: Try a theme on before you keep it
config.overviewNewFeatureThemePreviewWhat: Finding out what a theme looked like meant switching to it, then switching back if you did not like it — and doing that again for the next one.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemePreviewEnable: Nothing to switch on. Your choice is only saved once you pick one.
config.overviewNewFeatureSettingsSearchTitle: Search finds every setting, not just the ones you have seen
config.overviewNewFeatureSettingsSearchWhat: Looking for “webhook” found nothing at all unless you happened to have opened that tab before, which is the opposite of what a search is for.
config.overviewNewFeatureSettingsSearchEnable: Nothing to switch on. Press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K anywhere in Config, or use Find settings under the section list.
config.overviewNewFeatureChangedSettingsTitle: See what you have changed from the standard
config.overviewNewFeatureChangedSettingsWhat: Working out why your dashboard behaves differently from the guide meant opening every tab and looking for a ↺ beside each setting.
config.overviewNewFeatureChangedSettingsEnable: Nothing to switch on. The line stays out of the way while everything is still standard.
config.overviewNewFeatureToolbarGroupsTitle: Every “show this button” box sits with the thing it controls
config.overviewNewFeatureToolbarGroupsWhat: Thirteen near-identical “Show the … button” tick boxes in a row, with no way to tell which meant the strip at the top and which the bar at the bottom.
config.overviewNewFeatureToolbarGroupsEnable: Nothing to switch on — the settings themselves are unchanged, only how they are arranged.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxExplainTitle: The inbox explains itself, and its numbers add up
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxExplainWhat: A snoozed link is hidden from the list but was still counted above it, so a tile reading 12 could open a list of 9 with nothing explaining the gap.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxExplainEnable: Nothing to switch on. An empty list now says which kind of empty it is, and long inboxes load as you scroll rather than a page per click.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStatsTitle: See how the whole collection is doing
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStatsWhat: The health view could describe one bookmark in detail and the whole set barely at all: twenty monitors meant twenty heartbeats and no answer to how the week went.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStatsEnable: Nothing to switch on, though the panel needs something monitored to describe. The trend line starts once you have opened the health view on two separate days.
config.overviewNewFeatureCaptureHow: Install nextDash as an app and it appears in your phone’s share sheet: share a link and it lands in the Inbox. On a desktop browser, Config → Help → Inbox builds a bookmarklet carrying this install’s own address. The same route takes a plain web address, so a launcher, a script or a hotkey can save to it too — the integrations folder has ready-made pieces for Raycast, Dropzone, Ulauncher, Alfred and Apple Shortcuts.
config.overviewNewFeatureDuplicateWhereHow: The check looks everywhere now. Two copies on one page are still refused; a copy on another page is a question instead — “You already saved this on Work · Docs”, with the existing bookmark one click away and Save anyway if you meant it. The same document filed with work and with reference is a real thing to want, so the choice stays yours.
config.overviewNewFeatureRotReportHow: A row now says how long it has been failing, the list can be grouped by site so one host down reads as one problem, a monitored check can spot the polite kind of disappearance, and a dead link can be pointed at its last archived copy with the original address kept in the note. Rot report in the toolbar adds it up: what has gone, what has moved, what has been failing for over a month, and what broke this week.
config.overviewNewFeatureReviewSessionHow: When enough links want attention, a card in the corner of the dashboard names what is waiting — “10 links to review: 4 broken, 3 never opened, 3 not opened in a year” — and Start runs a session over the worst ten. It ends: it says how many you dealt with, offers another ten while more are waiting, and Done for today puts the offer away until tomorrow. Skipping is not handling, so the count is honest.
config.overviewNewFeatureFreshHow: When a page you saved offers a feed, nextDash notes where it is while fetching previews and checks it on the background re-check interval. A bookmark then carries a small count of what has been published since you last opened it, and a Fresh collection lists those newest first. Opening the bookmark clears it — that is the whole of the read state. No article list, no titles: this is not a feed reader.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStableListHow: Usage costs nothing now — it is still counted under the Unused and Stale tiles, still named on the row, it simply no longer decides where the row sits — and nothing else in the order changes when you act on a row either. Where a filter does stop selecting it, opening one under Unused or re-checking one under Broken, the row keeps its place, dimmed and marked handled, until you change the filter, sort or search, or reload the report.
config.overviewNewFeatureTypeThenEnterHow: Nothing opens by itself any more. The list narrows as you type and Enter opens the top result, with an exact shortcut match leading the list — so a shortcut costs one keystroke more and behaves the same tomorrow as today. Letters only reach the grid once a row is selected, and the line you type into now shows the key that started it: > for search, : for commands, ? for the finders, with an × to clear.
config.overviewNewFeatureFailureReasonHow: Every failure records what went wrong — DNS, timeout, refused, TLS, content — and shows it wherever the outage appears. A failed check is tried once more five seconds later and only written down if it fails again. A recovery says how long it was down, a 30-day figure says how much history is actually behind it, and certificate warnings now come from every check rather than only from bookmarks set to Monitor.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxCountsHow: Every count follows the filter, the button becomes Mark shown read while something is narrowing the view, and a line under the list says how many links are asleep and when the first one wakes. A link you marked read by mistake can go back to unread, and the page description sits under the title.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpreadHow: Let a category spread and its bookmarks run across two or three columns instead of down one, at the same height as the blocks around it. How many columns it takes is not something you set: it follows from the items-per-category limit and how many bookmarks are in it, so it grows and shrinks with the category and never goes wider than the grid.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkUndoHow: The toast now offers Undo for eight seconds and puts every bookmark back in the position it held. A delete that fails puts them back on its own and says so. The trash still catches everything for 30 days after that.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksMenuHow: Right-click any row for one menu on that row: open it, copy the address, edit, move it to another page or category, change how often it is checked, pin it, or delete it. Right-click a row that is part of a selection and the menu switches to the whole selection, with the count named.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkSettingsHow: Ten settings of its own, including what a quick-added bookmark starts with, the interval a bookmark gets when you switch it to Monitor, how many rows a delete has to touch before it asks, what counts as "not opened in a while", and which archive service the archive links point at.
config.overviewNewFeatureUsageDataHow: Search takes added: and opened: with today, week, month or year — and opened:never. Your own collections can now use pinned, untagged, days since last opened and days since last changed, and a Recently added collection answers the one question the others never could.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowKeysHow: Shift + P pins, Shift + S shares, Shift + R opens the row in Health, and t filters to its tag. Ctrl/Cmd + Enter opens a bookmark in a new tab for that press alone, whatever your standing preference says. Pin also has a right-click entry now.
config.overviewNewFeatureRowTagsHow: Switch on tags in the grid and the first two appear on the row, with the rest collapsing into a count. They give way before the bookmark name does, and stay out of the way on a phone.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxTagsHow: Tags now sit on the row. Click one to see only that tag, and click it again to go back. Right-click a link and choose Tags to edit them, search matches them along with the title and note, and both the CSV and JSON exports carry them.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxStatsHow: The Stats button in the Inbox toolbar shows how many links you have added, promoted and deleted, what share of the ones you decided on became bookmarks, and how long a link sits there before you deal with it.
config.overviewNewFeatureSpacingHow: Config → Appearance → Layout now has Category spacing and Page margins, each with Snug, Balanced and Airy.
config.overviewNewFeatureStructureTrashHow: Both now go to the trash for 30 days. A page is one entry — listed as “Page · 12 bookmarks” — and restoring brings the page, its categories and its bookmarks back in a single action.
config.overviewNewFeatureCategoryGridHow: A + sits beside the A–Z / Rec chips in a category header, and holding c does the same from the keyboard. Both act on the page on screen, so neither asks which page you meant.
config.overviewNewFeaturePageOverviewHow: Press , for the overview and use the New page row under the list — by click, by n, or by arrowing one stop past the last page.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthBulkHow: Tick the box on any row, or press x to tick the one under the cursor and move on, X for everything the filter shows. A bar appears above the list with Set checking, Re-check, Open, Copy links and Delete.
config.overviewNewFeatureBulkTagsHow: Select some rows and press the toolbar’s Tags button. Every tag you already use is listed, with a tick when the whole selection has it and “on 2 of 3” when only some do.
config.overviewNewFeatureFormCreateHow: Both dropdowns in the bookmark form lead with ➕ New page… and ➕ New category…. Picking one swaps the dropdown for a name box, and the new page or category is selected when you come back.
config.overviewNewFeatureMultiSelectHow: Press x to tick the row under the cursor, X for the whole category, Shift+↑/↓ for a range, Ctrl/Cmd+A for everything on screen — or Alt+click and Shift+click with the mouse. Select is in the right-click menu too.
config.overviewNewFeatureTrashHow: Restore puts a bookmark back on its own page at its old position. Delete forever and Empty trash clear it early.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthContextMenuHow: Right-click any row in the Health view to open that same menu at the cursor, the way a bookmark on the dashboard already did. Shift and right-click still gives you the browser’s own menu.
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitorEmphasisHow: Right-click a bookmark and pick Show in Health to jump straight to its row, from the dashboard or from Config → Bookmarks.
config.overviewNewFeatureSideRailHow: Pick a position under Config → Appearance → Button bar, or run :buttonbar from the command palette. The bar moves as you choose — no reload.
config.overviewNewFeatureNewsStreamHow: The chips above the list narrow it to one source, or hide the site's posts entirely. A green dot marks what arrived since you last read it, and All news & features opens the whole list under About.
config.overviewNewFeaturePreviewCardHow: Hover a bookmark. Shift + V keeps the card open with Copy, Refresh and Edit, and Esc closes it. A line with nothing to say is left out, so a bare link is a short card rather than empty space.
config.overviewNewFeatureButtonBarTabHow: Appearance → Button bar holds both halves: the five positions, each drawn as the page with the bar in it, and under them the main buttons and the extras with Show all, Hide all and a count. Toolbar & tabs keeps the header row, which is a different strip.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkFormHow: Press +, Shift+B, or Ctrl+Shift+A to open the form. Use Create + New to save and immediately add another; the grid updates behind the modal.
config.overviewNewFeatureUpdateCheckHow: Press Check for updates in the ★ modal header or on Config → Overview. When a newer release exists, open GitHub from the notice or dismiss it until the next version.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarksFiltersHow: Type in the search box (shortcuts match too), pick page or category from the dropdowns, or click a page, category, or tag on a row. Sort by last opened, most opened, or pinned first. Tick rows for bulk favicon refresh or CSV export.
config.overviewNewFeaturePagesTagsTabsHow: Use [ and ] to cycle sub-tabs from anywhere in config, or click Categories or Tags in the strip. Pages, Finders, and Collections follow after.
config.overviewNewFeatureRandomThemeHow: Choose Off (always your saved theme), On page refresh (new pick on each reload), or On view change (new pick when switching between bookmarks, config, inbox, health, or dashboard pages). With auto dark mode, only matching light or dark variants are eligible. While random is on, a Currently showing hint names the active theme.

config.helpFindersBody:
Finders are search shortcuts that send a query straight to an external site instead of searching your bookmarks. ?g nextdash searches Google for “nextdash”; ?w might go to Wikipedia. Open finder mode with ? or from the toolbar, and a fresh install starts with DuckDuckGo on du.

The point is the round trip you skip: no loading the site, finding its search box, then typing. One prefix and your text goes where it was always going.

Defining your own under Pages & tags → Finders takes three things: a shortcut, a display name, and a URL with %s where the query belongs. To get the URL, run any search on the site and copy the address, then replace what you searched for with %s:

  • Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%s
  • GitHub — https://github.com/search?q=%s
  • Your own docs, an internal wiki, a ticket tracker — anything with a search URL works, including sites only reachable on your own network.

Multi-word queries are encoded for you, so ?w keyboard layout behaves as typing it into the site itself would. Leave the query off entirely — just ?w — and you land on the site’s own search page.

Names and shortcuts have to be unique. Two finders answering to ?g would leave which one runs down to chance, so a duplicate is refused as you type it rather than accepted and quietly ignored later.

Tags can be attached to a finder, which keeps a long list navigable once you have more than a handful. nextDash also counts how often each is used, so the ones you actually reach for rise to the top of the list.

Blending them into ordinary search. Turn on Include finders in search under Behavior → Search and finders appear alongside bookmarks in normal > results — so one keystroke can reach either, without deciding up front whether you are looking for something you saved or something you want to look up.
config.helpCommandsBody:
: opens the command palette — actions rather than destinations. A lone : lists everything grouped by area, with the commands you use most floating to the top, so the palette gets shorter as it learns what you reach for. Type to narrow, Enter to run.

Many commands take an argument and complete as you type, so you rarely have to remember exact wording — :op is enough to be offered the :open … family. The space between a command and its argument is a space: it used to run the highlighted row instead, so a command taking an argument could not be finished by typing.

Opening several at once. These open real browser tabs, so a large selection opens a lot of them:

  • :open last 5 — reopen what you opened most recently. 3, 5 and 10 are offered; any number works.
  • :open tag work · :open category news — everything carrying a tag, or in a category
  • :open pinned — every pinned bookmark
  • :open all — everything on the current page. Worth a glance at the count first.

Finding and filtering without leaving the palette:

  • :tag work — list bookmarks with a tag in the palette, dashboard untouched
  • :filter / :filter clear — apply or drop a dashboard tag filter
  • :find / :find clear — the same for a text filter
  • :recent · :saved · :history — what you opened lately, and what you kept
  • :duplicates · :stale 30 — the two cleanup lists, without opening health

Changing how it looks, which is quicker than opening config and easy to undo:

  • :theme · :dark — switch theme or force dark
  • :layout modern · :density compact · :columns 4 — try a look without committing to it
  • :sort — change the sort mode of the focused category
  • :preview · :animations · :opacity — toggle the smaller visual settings

Housekeeping and getting somewhere:

  • :favicons fetch — re-download every bookmark’s icon
  • :backup · :export — open backups, or download an export straight away
  • :health refresh · :health broken — re-check availability, or jump to what is broken
  • :inbox · :inbox triage — open the inbox, or start working through it
  • :page new · :category new — create one without a trip to config
  • :goto config · :goto health · :goto stats — jump straight to a view
  • :note — edit a bookmark’s note in place
  • :cheat · :help · :whatsnew — the cheat sheet, this guide, or the release notes

The palette is the fastest way to reach anything you do occasionally, but not often enough to remember where it lives.

config.bookmarksPageFilterPromoBody: Pick a page to see only its bookmarks and categories. The address bar becomes a link you can share (#config/bookmarks/…).
config.overviewNewFeatureKeyboardHow: Use j/k or arrow keys on the section rail, [ and ] for sub-tabs, and list keys on Pages & tags and Bookmarks. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K opens Find settings.
config.overviewNewFeatureFindSettingsHow: Press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K anywhere in config, or click Find settings below Help in the left nav. Type to filter, then Enter to go.
config.overviewNewFeatureBookmarkPagesHow: Choose a page in the filter dropdown to scope categories and deep-link with #config/bookmarks/<pageId>. With All pages, categories show as Page · Category.
config.appearanceDisplayQuickNote: Everyday bookmark row options. Toolbar and tab visibility live on their own tab.
config.tipAddAnywhere: Shift+B opens the new-bookmark form from anywhere on the dashboard, even while something else has focus.
config.tipAddCapture: Install nextDash as an app and it appears in your phone's share sheet; on a desktop browser the bookmarklet under Help → Inbox saves the page you are looking at.
config.tipAddDuplicate: Saving a link you already have on another page tells you where it is and offers to open it — Save anyway keeps the second copy when you meant it.
config.cheatsheetPdfHint: Every keyboard shortcut, ready to print (opens in a new tab)
config.bookmarksTagCloudHint: Filter by one or more tags
config.shortcutTooltipsLabel: Show shortcut hints on toolbar icons

When enabled, hovering a header link or toolbar button shows its name and keyboard shortcut.

• Helps you learn the keys
• Turn off for a quieter dashboard

Also available as :shortcuts on|off in the command panel.
config.statsAxisShareHealthy: Healthy share of {total} tracked bookmarks — 0% to 100%
config.statsActivityLifetimeHint: Counted over the whole life of these bookmarks, not only this period — nextDash stores a total per bookmark, not a date for every open.
config.statsActivityNote: Each bar counts the bookmarks whose last use falls in that period. A bookmark appears once, on the day you last opened it.
config.statsEmptyBody: Statistics fill in as you add bookmarks and start opening them. Add a few and this page will have something to say.

config.statsHeadlineShortcuts: You reach for bookmarks by keystroke: {pct}% carry a shortcut, against {tagPct}% carrying tags.
config.statsHeadlineTags: You organise by tag: {pct}% of bookmarks carry one, against {shortcutPct}% carrying a shortcut.

config.statsHeadlineBroad: Your usage is spread out: {used} of {total} bookmarks have been opened, with no small group dominating.
config.statsHeadlineUnused: Nothing has been opened yet, so there is no habit to read from this collection.

config.logRetentionHintCount: Only the newest entries are kept; older ones drop off as new lines arrive. Age is not considered in this mode.
config.logRetentionHint: Older lines are dropped automatically. The newest lines are always kept, whatever the age limit.

config.logDetailLiveNormal: docker logs is now showing what the server does, from the next line onwards.

config.logFloorQuiet: Recording at Quiet — only problems are kept, so this list will be short.
config.logFloorNormal: Recording at Normal — debug lines are not kept.
config.logFloorVerbose: Recording at Verbose — every step is kept.
config.logChannelsHint: A machine-readable record of what happened, kept apart from the readable lines above. Pick what belongs in it.
config.logClearConfirm: Delete every stored log line? The file on disk goes too, and this cannot be undone.
config.logLoadFailed: Could not read the server log.
config.trashIntro: Deleted bookmarks, pages and categories stay here for {days} days, then go for good.
config.trashRestorePageIdTaken: A different page now uses that page’s slot, so it cannot be restored without replacing it.
config.trashRestorePageGone: That bookmark’s page no longer exists. It stays in the trash — recreate the page, then restore it.
config.trashEmptyConfirm: Permanently delete everything in the trash?
config.overviewNewFeatureMonitoringHow: Press c on a row in Health and choose Monitor. The server then checks it on its own interval, whether or not you have the dashboard open, and the row grows a heartbeat, an uptime percentage and an outage history. Say what "up" means for that page with a keyword or specific status codes, watch for it quietly turning into a different page, and get an alert on Slack, Telegram, Pushover and others when it goes down.
config.overviewNewFeatureWorkThroughHow: Open Health and press f, or use the Work through button. One bookmark fills the screen with its actions large — re-check, open, delete, skip — and j and k move between them. Esc leaves you on the row you had reached, so dipping in for three fixes and back out is not a mode switch.
config.overviewNewFeatureThemePreviewHow: Open the Theme list under Appearance and move through it: the dashboard behind takes on each theme as you go. Press Esc or click away and you are back where you started. There are 23 new themes to look through as well.
config.overviewNewFeatureSettingsSearchHow: Every setting is searchable the moment you open Config, and settings answer to more than their exact label — “uptime”, “wallpaper” and “hotkey” each find the right one even though those words are nowhere on screen.
config.overviewNewFeatureChangedSettingsHow: At a glance now says how many settings differ from the standard and takes you to them. Each tab of settings gained Only changed, and each group a Reset panel that puts the whole lot back at once.
config.overviewNewFeatureToolbarGroupsHow: The header strip keeps its group under Toolbar & tabs; the two halves of the button bar sit on the Button bar tab, under the control that says where the bar goes. Each group has Show all and Hide all with a count of what is showing.
config.overviewNewFeatureInboxExplainHow: Every count now means what you can act on right now, every pill carries its own, and a sentence under the toolbar says what the active filter selects. The ℹ beside Triage covers snoozing, promoting and the rest.
config.overviewNewFeatureHealthStatsHow: The Monitored filter now opens with pooled uptime across every monitor, the least available ones, anything slower than last week, and every outage. The header draws the share of healthy bookmarks over the last 90 days.
config.ptViewOnlySorted: View only — the saved order is unchanged. Clear the sort to move rows again.
config.ptViewOnlyFiltered: View only — clear the search to move rows again.
config.maintenanceNote: Times when downtime is expected — a nightly backup, a weekly reboot. Checks still run and the heartbeat still records what happened, but failures inside a window raise no alert and do not count against uptime.
config.maintenanceEmpty: No windows. Alerts fire whenever a monitored bookmark goes down.
config.maintenanceIncomplete: Set a start and end time — an incomplete window is ignored.
config.maintenanceSameTime: Start and end are the same, so this window covers nothing and is ignored.
config.maintenanceWraps: Runs past midnight into the next day.

config.trashRestoredSomeFailed: Restored {ok}. {failed} could not be restored and stay in the trash.
config.trashLoadFailed: The trash could not be loaded.

config.bookmarksGroupNewNote: What a bookmark added with & or + starts out as.
config.bookmarksGroupBulkNote: When to ask first, and what counts as neglected.
config.bulkFaviconConfirm: Fetch icons for {n} bookmarks? This can take a while.
config.configBookmarksSortInfoMessage: The order this list is in when you open it. Health and the Inbox remember their sort; this one used to start on page order every time.
config.configBookmarksPageSizeInfoMessage: How many rows are added each time you reach the end of the list. Lower is lighter on a phone; higher gives more overview during a clean-up.
config.bookmarkDeleteConfirmFromInfoMessage: Deleting this many rows or more asks first. Set it higher to work through a clean-up without a dialog each time — every delete still offers an undo and stays in the trash for 30 days.
config.defaultMonitorIntervalInfoMessage: The interval a bookmark gets when you switch it to Monitor without choosing one, including in bulk.
config.newBookmarkCheckModeInfoMessage: What a quick-added bookmark starts on. Useful if you run services and want each one checked from the moment you add it.
config.newBookmarkPinnedInfoMessage: Whether a quick-added bookmark is pinned to the top of its category straight away.
config.bookmarkStaleDaysInfoTitle: When a bookmark counts as neglected
config.bookmarkStaleDaysInfoMessage: Used by the statistics and by the clean-up score that tells you a page needs attention. A daily work library is neglected sooner than a reference archive.
config.bulkFaviconConfirmFromInfoTitle: When to confirm an icon refresh
config.bulkFaviconConfirmFromInfoMessage: Fetching icons for this many selected rows asks first, the way the whole-dashboard refresh does. Zero never asks.
config.bookmarkArchiveUrlInfoMessage: Where "Find in Web Archive" sends a bookmark. {url} is replaced with its address, so a self-hosted ArchiveBox or archive.today works too.
config.showRowTagsInfoMessage: Adds a small chip per tag beside the bookmark name, the same chip the Inbox and Config → Bookmarks use. Off by default: a row with several tags is busier, and the grid earns its keep by staying scannable. Tags never push the name out — they give way first, and are hidden on a phone.
config.logActivityHint: What was done — bookmarks saved, pages added, checks run — mixed into the same log as the requests. Pick Activity only to read just those, or turn categories on and off with NEXTDASH_ACTIVITY_LOG.
config.statsNoActivityEver: Nothing has been opened yet, so there is nothing to plot. This fills in as you use your bookmarks.
config.statsScopeWholeLibrary: These figures cover the whole library, not just {page}.
config.statsHealthTrendWaiting: A day is recorded each time the health report runs. Once there are a few, the change over time appears here.
config.backupRotationNote: The newest {keep} are kept. Making another — or restoring, which copies the current data first — removes the oldest.
config.aboutFeatureCatalogue: Everything else you can switch on
config.aboutFeatureCatalogueNote: Settings from earlier releases, in the order they were written down.
config.aboutTrackTitle: Follow it from your own dashboard
config.aboutTrackNote: Save nextdash.cc as a bookmark and Fresh counts what it publishes, the same way it does for every other page you keep.
config.aboutTrackDone: nextdash.cc is already one of your bookmarks — Fresh will count new posts on it like any other page.
config.aboutTrackAdded: nextdash.cc is on your dashboard. Turn Fresh on under Behavior → Fresh to see what it publishes.
config.aboutIntro: What nextDash is, and where it comes from.
config.helpTipsIntro: Small things that save a keystroke, grouped by what you are doing. The dashboard shows one of these above the buttons when you switch that on.
config.helpCopyLink: Copy a link to this topic
config.helpLinkInAddressBar: The link is in the address bar.
config.sessionTipsInfoMessage:
A single shortcut hint rotates above the button bar, changing daily.

• On: one tip at a time, dismissible
• Off: nothing above the buttons

The full catalogue is in Config → Help → Tips either way.
config.monitorNotifyUrlInfoMessage:
The address the server posts to when a monitored bookmark goes down or comes back.

For a webhook this is the full URL your service gave you. For Pushover, leave it empty and fill in the two token fields instead.

The server posts from itself, so the address has to be reachable from where nextDash runs, not from your browser.
config.faviconRefreshPolicyInfoMessage:
How often a bookmark icon is re-downloaded from its site.

• Never: keep what is stored until you refresh by hand
• Monthly or Weekly: replace icons that have gone stale
• Every load: always current, and a request per bookmark per visit

Sites change their icons rarely, so Never or Monthly suits most collections.
config.usageAnalyticsInfoMessage:
Off unless you turn it on. When on, nextDash reports which features are used and roughly how large the collection is — every number rounded into a band, never bookmark names, addresses, searches or notes.

Switching it off stops the counting entirely rather than gathering and discarding it.

Every HTTPS check completes a handshake anyway, so the expiry date costs nothing to read. This is how far ahead the first warning appears.

One number rather than three: two tighter marks follow it in the same proportion the built-in ladder uses — a month ahead also warns at a week and at three days, a fortnight ahead at three days and at one. A certificate belongs to a host, so ten bookmarks on one domain warn once and a single renewal clears them all.

config.helpCaptureBody:
The browser extension covers Chrome and Chromium. Everywhere else — Safari, Firefox, a phone, a work laptop you cannot install anything on — there are two routes that need nothing installed. From a phone's share sheet. Install nextDash as an app (Add to Home Screen), and it appears in the share sheet of every app on the device. Sharing a link saves it to the inbox and opens nextDash on it. Android sometimes sends the address inside the text rather than as a link; nextDash picks it out either way. From any browser. The bookmarklet below saves the page you are looking at. Drag the button to your bookmarks bar, or copy the line and make a bookmark of it by hand. If this install has a write token, capture needs a token of its own: set NEXTDASH_CAPTURE_TOKEN on the server and paste it below. It opens nothing but these two routes, so a bookmarklet in someone else's browser history can at worst put a link in your inbox.

From a script, a launcher or a hotkey. The same route takes a plain GET /add?url=…&title=…, and the integrations/ folder in the repository carries ready-made pieces built on it: a shell script, two Raycast commands, a Dropzone action, a Ulauncher extension, and Alfred and Apple Shortcuts recipes.
